review_notes: I read the whole file and the definitions of Module.Basis.rightBaseChange, rightBaseChange_repr and rightBaseChange_apply in Definitions/Def_DedekindDomain_Completion_BaseChange.lean. The simp lemmas there only cover `b i ⊗ₜ x`. I also read the sibling file S_Algebra_trace_tensorProduct_rightActions_tmul_eq_algebraMap_trace_mul.lean. Mathlib has no `rightBaseChange` declarations, so nothing there competes with the lemma. I did not run Lean. The suggestion to add a simp attribute and move the lemma is untested, and I did not check for simp-set conflicts. Because `repr_tmul` is stated with `•`, a `Finsupp` application on the left and an explicit `Basis` argument, I expect it to be a safe, terminating simp rewrite. I did not suggest a simp attribute on `repr_map`: its LHS involves `Algebra.TensorProduct.map` on a general element, so it is a more specialised lemma and the case for it is weaker.

findings.excerpt:
theorem repr_tmul (b : Module.Basis n K L) (l : L) (x : B) (i : n) :
    (b.rightBaseChange L (B := B)).repr (l ⊗ₜ[K] x) i = b.repr l i • x := by
findings.problem: This is the canonical coordinate formula for `Module.Basis.rightBaseChange` on a general pure tensor `l ⊗ₜ x`. It is not a simp lemma and it is hidden in the helper namespace `NBCAux`. The only simp lemma for `(b.rightBaseChange A).repr`, `Module.Basis.rightBaseChange_repr`, covers only basis vectors `b i ⊗ₜ x`. So `simp` cannot compute `(b.rightBaseChange L).repr (l ⊗ₜ x) i` for general `l`. The file works around this with a manual `conv_lhs => rw [← b.sum_repr l]` followed by a long `simp only` list. The sibling file S_Algebra_trace_tensorProduct_rightActions_tmul_eq_algebraMap_trace_mul.lean rederives the same fact as its local `key`, again with `rw [Module.Basis.rightBaseChange_repr, Finsupp.single_apply]` and `Finset.sum_ite_eq'`. `solution` here also needs several explicit `rw`s (`Module.Basis.rightBaseChange_apply`, `NBCAux2.repr_map`) because no simp normal form exists for these coordinates.
findings.proposed_change: Move the lemma next to `Module.Basis.rightBaseChange_repr` in Definitions/Def_DedekindDomain_Completion_BaseChange.lean. Generalise it to `[CommSemiring A] [CommSemiring B]` there, and name it e.g. `Module.Basis.rightBaseChange_repr_tmul`. Mark it `@[simp]`, with RHS `b.repr l i • x`. Then reuse it both in `NBCAux2.repr_map` and in the trace file's `key`. Both `rw [NBCAux.repr_tmul, NBCAux.repr_tmul, ...]` and `key` collapse to `simp`. The existing `rightBaseChange_repr` stays consistent: on `b i ⊗ₜ x` the new rule gives `b.repr (b i) j • x`, which `Module.Basis.repr_self` and `Finsupp.single_apply` should reduce.
findings.benefit: There is one canonical simp-normal form for coordinates of pure tensors in the right base-change basis. The duplicated proofs in this file and the trace file go away. Later proofs about `Algebra.norm`, `Algebra.trace` or `leftMulMatrix` of tensors can use `simp` instead of re-deriving the sum-over-basis argument. The lemma becomes discoverable instead of being private to an auxiliary namespace.

evidence.excerpt: (b.rightBaseChange A).repr (b i ⊗ₜ x) = Finsupp.single i x
bA.repr (m ⊗ₜ[K] a) i = algebraMap K A (b.repr m i) * a
